description: Single-panel scatter chart (Fig. 19) compiling room-temperature tensile properties of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels. The x-axis is labelled "Yield/Tensile strength, MPa" and runs from 200 to 1600 with ticks every 200; the y-axis is labelled "Total elongation, %" and runs 0 to 100 with ticks every 10. Every alloy contributes one open symbol for yield strength and one filled symbol for tensile strength, as defined by the middle legend box on the right ("Yield strength" = open outline, "Tensile strength" = filled black). Symbol shape and colour encode Mn content in wt.%, per the lower-right legend: red triangle 12~18, magenta square 18~25, green triangle 25~28, orange hexagon 28~33. Dashed coloured ellipses enclose the data belonging to each phase constitution, per the upper-right legend: "Single austenit phase" (magenta, printed as "Single austenit phase"), "Single ferrite phase" (yellow), "Ferrite-austenite-MC/κ" (blue), "Austenite-based duplex" (purple) and "Ferrite-based duplex" (green). Three black dashed hyperbolae mark constant strength×elongation products labelled 70 GPa·%, 50 GPa·% and 30 GPa·%. Points spread along a diagonal band from low strength/high elongation to high strength/low elongation; the magenta single-austenite and purple austenite-based-duplex ellipses sit highest, the green ferrite-based duplex lowest. The figure demonstrates that Mn content and phase constitution jointly govern the strength–ductility trade-off of these steels.

observations.observation: The x-axis is labelled 'Yield/Tensile strength, MPa' and spans 200 to 1600 MPa with tick intervals of 200 MPa, so both yield and tensile strength values are plotted on the same axis.
The y-axis is labelled 'Total elongation, %' and spans 0 to 100% with tick intervals of 10%.
A legend box defines open symbols as 'Yield strength' and filled black symbols as 'Tensile strength', so each alloy appears as a paired open/filled marker of the same colour and shape.
Marker colour and shape encode Mn content in wt.%: red triangle = 12~18, magenta square = 18~25, green triangle = 25~28, orange hexagon = 28~33.

Dashed coloured ellipses delimit five data groups labelled in the legend as 'Single austenit phase' (magenta), 'Single ferrite phase' (yellow), 'Ferrite-austenite-MC/κ' (blue), 'Austenite-based duplex' (purple) and 'Ferrite-based duplex' (green).
Three black dashed curves crossing the data cloud are labelled 70 GPa·%, 50 GPa·% and 30 GPa·%, i.e. contours of constant strength × total elongation product.
Data points form a diagonal band running from roughly 400-600 MPa at 50-80% elongation down to about 1000-1600 MPa at 5-20% elongation, i.e. the characteristic trade-off ('banana') shape.

The magenta single-austenite and purple austenite-based duplex ellipses occupy the upper/high-product part of the plot, while the green ferrite-based duplex ellipse lies at low strength and low elongation (below the 30 GPa·% contour).
Individual data points cannot be attributed to specific references or to specific alloy compositions, because only Mn-content ranges and phase classes are labelled.

The caption states the figure shows the measured room-temperature tensile properties of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels with various Mn contents, compiled from references [15,23,34,51,52,79,80], [91e93], [120e150].

The citing text states that the strength–ductility relationship of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels follows a typical 'banana curve', and that single-austenite and austenite-based duplex (A-BDP) steels appear superior to the others.

The citing text gives Fe-30Mn-11Al-1.2C single-austenite steel as 1058 MPa yield strength, 1310 MPa tensile strength and 38% total elongation [137]; the plotted points do not carry this alloy's name, so the figure only corroborates that such a high-product point exists in the magenta ellipse.

The citing text states that fine intragranular and intergranular κ-carbide enhance yield strength without significantly deteriorating ductility but raise the yield ratio to >0.8 of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels.
The citing text states that higher Mn content expands the room available for improving strength and ductility but increases material cost and processing difficulty.

subfigures.description: Main scatter plot: x-axis 'Yield/Tensile strength, MPa' 200-1600, y-axis 'Total elongation, %' 0-100. Open symbols = yield strength, filled symbols = tensile strength; marker shape/colour codes Mn content in wt.%. Five dashed coloured ellipses group the data by phase constitution; three black dashed hyperbolae labelled 70, 50 and 30 GPa·% mark constant strength×elongation products.

Three stacked legend boxes: (top) phase-constitution key with dashed line samples for Single austenit phase, Single ferrite phase, Ferrite-austenite-MC/κ, Austenite-based duplex and Ferrite-based duplex; (middle) open box = Yield strength, filled box = Tensile strength; (bottom) 'Mn content, wt.%' key with red triangle 12~18, magenta square 18~25, green triangle 25~28, orange hexagon 28~33.

Heavy marker overlap in the central 600-1000 MPa region prevents counting or separating individual alloys
